newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse hits new all-time record high.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse hits new all-time record high.

text.p: German shares hit a new all-time high in floor dealings on Wednesday, catching up with records made in Tuesday's post-bourse electronic trade after the dollar came off lows against the mark.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares reached an all-time high of 2,773.10 points and then came off slightly to trade up 37.98 points, or 1.39 percent, at 2,772.28 by 1030 GMT.
Tuesday's late IBIS rally had come after comments by Bundesbank council member Edgar Meister that the dollar trading below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate", boosted the U.S. currency.
Bourse dealings, particularly in export-oriented chemicals and carmaker shares, had been held back by the weak dollar, which had been trading at a two-month low near 1.49 marks.

The dollar got another boost after the IBIS close on comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that the dollar was once again on its way higher and that he always welcomed the dollar being at its correct level.
After Tietmeyer's comments the dollar pulled above the crucial 1.50 mark level and on Wednesday climbed further to around 1.5070 marks, further encouraging German stocks.
But dealers said they saw momentum lessening. "The rally is feeding the rally, but today with somewhat less foaming at the mouth," said one dealer.
Shares in the spotlight on Wednesday were utility giant Veba AG and chemicals and drugs group BASF AG, both reporting nine month results.
But while Veba's figures pleased the market, sending the stock up almost five three percent, or 3.90 marks to 87.50 marks, BASF's disappointed and the stock fell 24 pfennigs to 51.10 marks.
